charts.title: Fit math — NVFP4 weights ×1.18 vs Spark budgets
charts.caption: Computed with lab03_fit_math.py from the runbook formula (§1.2): Nano ≈19.5 GB and Super ≈77.9 GB fit one 115 GB-usable Spark at NVFP4; Ultra ≈357 GB exceeds even two Sparks (230 GB) — cloud-only.

charts.title: What one 128 GB Spark can hold, by precision
charts.caption: Runbook §1.2 memory rule of thumb (weights ×1.18 overhead, ~90% usable): quantization is why Super needs Q4/NVFP4 while Nano is comfortable at Q8. Long agentic contexts eat another 10–30 GB of KV-cache.

charts.title: Family reference throughput on a Spark
charts.caption: From the demos/step01_family.py reference table — simulated GB10 figures, illustrative; single-stream decode on a Spark is bounded by its 273 GB/s memory bandwidth, so measure your own endpoint.
